statement: For all natural numbers $m$, $n$, and $p$, iterating the map $x \mapsto n + x$ a total of $m$ times, starting from the base value $p$, yields exactly $m \cdot n + p$. In other words, the $m$-fold iterated addition of $n$ onto an arbitrary initial value $p$ computes $m \cdot n + p$, so multiplication arises as iterated addition even in the presence of a non-zero starting offset.
